record_notes.DCP-LETT-1551: Incoming Sulivan incomplete letter, February 2 with 1855 supplied from winter dispersal discussions. Four surviving paragraphs, salutation, six footnotes, separate Darwin annotations and bibliography read. Family illness acknowledgement does not date personal receipt. Only mainland vegetation remembered on Falkland shores was chiefly birch trees, abundant on southwest-facing coast and used for Arrow and Philomel fuel; most seasoned and barkless for years, some rooted, other broken branches only probably storm-torn. Beagle paint spoilage recalled but seeds versus dust explicitly unknown. Snipe winter departure and no remembered strange birds are separate from woodcock seen on homeward merchant ship in August southeast trades. Bird could not be caught, struck ship and fell into sea. Position forgotten: more than 500 miles from nearest land, Azores, and more than 1000 from other land are recollected distances, not coordinates. Darwin brown-crayon scores, inserted strange and portfolio 18 are undated later layers, not independently dated Sulivan prose. No surviving Darwin inquiry or specific dated outgoing use of this 1855 report found in the preserved current corpus. Earlier Sulivan mathematical/geological sources have their own previous accepted relationships and do not supply this missing question.

Do not correct source one-twelfth to editorial one-thirteenth or silently modernize units. Letter reached old Falmouth address; writer left two months ago, not Darwin receipt. Health/promotion hopes not later1841 promotion knowledge. Separate cover calculations240x6/240x7 by Darwin undated. Tables/fractions require faithful layout reconstruction.

record_notes.DCP-LETT-730: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. January13–February12,1845 serial incoming letter with18 embedded drawings. Opening autograph1844 is erroneous: later February12.45 and calendar establish1845, not first-ID order. P1–12 January13 initial hurried Gallegos fossil collecting and provisional grey-sandstone attribution; P13 January14 explicitly retracts that bed assignment and distinguishes clay(c) above sandstone(d). All fossil identifications remain tentative, much material broken and collected from fallen blocks rather than in situ. P14–15 January29 WestFalkland soundings/map and trap dykes; map explicitly by eye. P16–21 February3 onward report colt mortality, fox comparison, corrected north-side ice-formation locality, health anecdotes, fossils/shell casts and geological conjectures. P22 includes undated preceding shell-cast continuation, then internal Stanley February12.45 heading; divide at its exact normalized character offset. Later section is third-party Council-member hearsay about FitzRoy, not independent facts or Darwin voice. Colour cliff sketch described P19 is composite within a mile, not exact one spot; inline figures do not prove preservation of separate original watercolour. Cover inscription is Sulivan text, not instructions. All Darwin annotations undated; neither writing instalments nor later annotations establish Darwin receipt. June4 witness864 establishes known-by for fossil news, not exact arrival. July886 expects reply but no outgoing Sulivan response survives in this packet.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-886: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. July4,1845 Montevideo. Delays return at least a year; retains main fossil casks unless a suitable direct steamer, sends small sample box by THIS packet, marks matching fragments with three cuts, separates white-paper armour/bone from surface shingle and SaundersIsland shell casts. Dispatch is not Darwin receipt; no whole-cask arrival claim. Met Rugendas yesterday July3, planned publication not later1855–58 publication knowledge. P3 hopes next packet brings reply to prior Falkland letter730; own prior letter is not a conversational answer. Political predictions remain opinions, family departures and return estimates remain plans. No surviving Darwin response established.
